standard_prerequisites.use: The characterization of quasi-finiteness at a point as an isolated fibre point under finite type (Morphisms, cited in the statement footnote) and the affine algebra case (Algebra, etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-one-prime); cited inputs with the localization reduction written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Choose affine opens Y in X and W in S with x in Y and f(Y) contained in W.
Verify x remains an isolated point of a fibre of the restricted morphism Y -> W.
Show the conclusion for Y -> W implies the conclusion for f.
Conclude by the cited affine algebra case for the one-prime situation.

proof_roadmap.step: Restrict to affine opens containing x and track isolation of the fibre point.
Descend the conclusion from the affine case cited in Algebra.

difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S locally of finite type and a point x whose image fibre point is isolated (i.e. f quasi-finite at x), the lemma produces an elementary etale neighbourhood (U, u) -> (S, s) and an open V of the base change X_U such that V -> U is finite, u has a unique preimage v in V, and kappa(v) = kappa(x) over x; moreover the triple pulls back to any further elementary etale neighbourhood of (U, u). The retained proof is a written affine-localization reduction: choose affine opens Y of X and W of S with f(Y) in W containing x, note x stays isolated in the fibre of the restricted map Y -> W, check that the statement for the restriction implies the statement for f, and invoke the algebra chapter's affine one-prime case. Retained author proof at lines 11955-11963.
